title: Time Management · Do / Does
subtitle: Outcomes Workbook: workplace vocabulary, negatives and questions

blocks.title: Time-management vocabulary
blocks.text: Complete each sentence with one word or phrase. Example: I have an appointment at 10.

items.prompt: Here's the ___ of orders we need to send out.
Production's in a ___ to get them ready.
The Bancroft order's a ___, so they must finish that one first.
You've got an ___ with Mr Jennings at 10am.
Can you ___ it for this afternoon, please?
I'll need to ___ tonight and finish it.
Let's ___ the meeting until tomorrow.
I need to ___ — bring me some coffee, please.

blocks.title: Make the sentences negative
blocks.text: Rewrite the whole sentence in the negative. Example: She works here. → She doesn’t work here.

items.prompt: I've got an appointment with the sales manager this morning.
items.answer: I haven't got an appointment with the sales manager this morning.
items.explanation: I haven't got an appointment with the sales manager this morning.

items.prompt: We're working on the new project this afternoon.
items.answer: We aren't working on the new project this afternoon.
items.explanation: We aren't working on the new project this afternoon.

items.prompt: There's a meeting next Friday to discuss progress.
items.answer: There isn't a meeting next Friday to discuss progress.
items.explanation: There isn't a meeting next Friday to discuss progress.

items.prompt: My contract ends in two months.
items.answer: My contract doesn't end in two months.
items.explanation: My contract doesn't end in two months.

items.prompt: Jorge is attending a training course tomorrow.
items.answer: Jorge isn't attending a training course tomorrow.
items.explanation: Jorge isn't attending a training course tomorrow.

items.prompt: I'm leaving work at the end of this month.
items.answer: I'm not leaving work at the end of this month.
items.explanation: I'm not leaving work at the end of this month.

blocks.title: Do or Does?
blocks.text: Choose the auxiliary that agrees with the subject. Example: ___ she work here? → Does

items.prompt: ___ you usually take a break at noon?
___ she arrange all the meetings?
What ___ they prioritise at work?
___ your manager often stay up late?
___ the team have a meeting every Monday?
How often ___ you rush in the mornings?

blocks.title: don't or doesn't?
blocks.text: Choose the correct negative auxiliary. Example: He ___ work nights. → doesn't

items.prompt: She ___ rush in the mornings — she always plans ahead.
I ___ have an appointment today, so I'm free.
They ___ take a break until 3 pm.
The project ___ end until next year.
We ___ delay meetings — we always reschedule them properly.
My boss ___ stay up late — she leaves at 5 every day.

blocks.title: Write the question
blocks.text: Use the underlined information from the answer to make a question. Example: She arranges the meetings. → Who arranges the meetings?

items.prompt: I usually take a break at 2 pm. → Ask about the time.
items.answer: When do you usually take a break?
items.explanation: When do you usually take a break?

items.prompt: My manager prioritises the urgent contracts first. → Ask who.
items.answer: Who prioritises the urgent contracts first?
items.explanation: Who prioritises the urgent contracts first?

items.prompt: They delay meetings because of the rush. → Ask why.
She stays up late twice a week. → Ask how often.
items.answer: How often does she stay up late?
items.explanation: How often does she stay up late?

items.prompt: I arrange appointments in the morning. → Ask when.
